# Cases whose comparison with the node oracle is not "ok" (see expect_test.go).
# id<TAB>status<TAB>reason
axis-tickCount-day	node-error	upstream throws in the renderer, not in the layout: `tickCount` is an interval string on a band scale, so AxisTicks (vega-encode) raises "Only time and utc scales accept interval strings." (vega-scale tickCount); vega-dataflow's evaluate stops the whole pulse there, leaving each axis group's items array with holes for the marks that had not run (axis-grid, axis-ticks, axis-labels), and SVGStringRenderer.mark then reads `.marktype` of the undefined hole and throws (vega-scenegraph visit). The engine stops the pulse at the same operator and builds the same partial scene, but its scene graph has no holes, so it renders; upstream's scene with the holes filtered out serialises to byte-identical SVG, so the crash is an upstream serialisation artifact the engine does not reproduce
